subject: Rollover & prepay path for CrestEdge renewal — buydown proposal
body:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Blake <carolyn@crestedge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rollover & prepay path for CrestEdge renewal — buydown proposal

Hi Carolyn / Samir,

Thanks again for the time last week. Based on our conversation and your indicated preference for predictable budget impact, I put together a short rollover/prepay option that balances an up-front credit with an ongoing true-up so you can scale without surprise overages. Draft attached: CrestEdge_Rollover_Summary_20270919.pdf.

High level — three options we can move quickly on:
- 36-month co-term with front-loaded prepay (preferred if procurement wants predictable spend)
- 24-month with higher year-1 prepay and annual true-ups
- 12-month with a mid-contract conversion to a staged annualization

If you confirm interest in the 36-month path I can put together a buydown schedule (example: 50% prepay year 1 => 10% unit buydown; 25% prepay year 2 => 5% buydown) and an early true-up cadence (quarterly). I attached a pricing model (redwood-pricing-buydown-model.xlsx) to show sensitivity.

Can you confirm:
1) Procurement target date (you mentioned late Oct)
2) Whether CrestEdge requires PO or DocuSign approach
3) Any internal approval thresholds (discount >7% needs exec okay)

Happy to set a 30-min call with procurement next week to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Samir and I will review the attached model and get back. If you can send a pared-down one-pager we can circulate internally that would help.

Subject: Fwd: Rollover & prepay path for CrestEdge renewal — need pricing guidance

Team — forwarding Carolyn's note. Procurement target is the week of Oct 18–22. They like the idea of a 3-year with 50% prepay year1 and quarterly true-ups. They also asked about invoice cadence (they prefer Jan/Apr/Jul).

Can you advise:
- feasible buydown ladder (units / % off) we can pitch without needing legal price concessions?
- recommended exec approval threshold (I expect they may push for ~12% aggregate discount if we front-load credits)
- rounding on numbers to make a clean one-pager for procurement

I've attached our pricing workbook: redwood-pricing-buydown-model.xlsx and a preliminary term table (CrestEdge_Prelim_Term_Table.csv). I want to propose a standard DocuSign route unless legal asks for PO.

Thanks — Sofia

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rollover & prepay path for CrestEdge renewal — need pricing guidance

Sofia — my suggested structure below (numbers are illustrative, see attached workbook for line-item math):

Proposal (recommended): 36-month co-term, yearly billing but customer can elect 3 invoice dates (Jan/Apr/Jul) — we will align payment schedule to their preferred cadence.

Pricing ladder:
- Year 1: 50% prepay of committed units -> 10% unit price buydown applied pro rata across consumed tokens.
- Year 2: 25% prepay -> additional 5% buydown.
- Year 3: no prepay required; CPI-style uplift capped at 3%/yr.

True-up and overspend: quarterly true-ups with settlement; any overage beyond committed units charged at standard list (no retro discount).

Concessions: we can go to aggregate 12% effective discount if procurement signs 50% prepay + a 36-month term and agrees to quarterly true-ups. Anything >12% requires VP approval (request by Marissa).

Ask: allow a 7% one-time onboarding credit if they accept DocuSign and sign by Oct 20. This helps get contract across the finish line.

Attached: redwood-pricing-buydown-model.xlsx (worked examples), CrestEdge_Prelim_Term_Table.csv.

If Sofia wants, I can draft the one-pager for procurement — will keep it single page with the ladder and payment cadence.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Blake <carolyn@crestedge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rollover & prepay path for CrestEdge renewal — buydown proposal

Carolyn / Samir — thank you for the quick reply and timing. Based on internal alignment here is a concise one-pager proposal and next steps (attached and pasted below).

Quick proposal summary:
- Term: 36 months co-term (Oct 2027 -> Sep 2030)
- Prepay: 50% of year-1 committed units payable on signature -> 10% unit buydown applied to consumed units in year 1
- Year 2 prepay 25% -> 5% additional buydown
- True-up: quarterly, settlement invoices applied to following invoice cycle
- Invoice cadence: we will support Jan/Apr/Jul invoices aligned to CrestEdge's preference (finance to confirm exact dates)
- Onboarding credit: 7% one-time credit if signed by Oct 20 (DocuSign preferred)
- Approval: we can move to an aggregate 12% effective discount without further exec sign-off; anything above requires VP approval.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred invoice dates (Jan/Apr/Jul OK?)
2) Confirm DocuSign signatory or PO process (if PO required we will route legal and alter timelines)
3) If agreed, we'll send a DocuSign envelope (pre-filled with the 36-month amendment and payment schedule). Link: DocuSign_CrestEdge_3yr_Proposal.link

I've attached: CrestEdge_Rollover_Summary_20270919.pdf (one-pager) and the pricing workbook. If you'd like, Marissa can join a short procurement call to walk the numbers.

If we can get sign-off by Oct 20 we can align the Jan invoice to start the committed usage window.

Best,
Sofia
